page: Microsoft Azure D32plds_v6 is a Dpldsv6-family virtual machine powered by a Microsoft Neoverse-N2 ARM processor. Operating on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor, this server features 32 dedicated physical cores and 32 vCPUs running at 3.4 GHz, with a single thread per core. The processor is equipped with 64 KB of L1d cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 128 MB of L3 cache. It includes 64.0 GB of system memory, yielding a resource density of 2.0 GB of RAM per core. Storage is provided via a bundled 1890 GB local disk, and the instance is Premium Storage capable. No GPU accelerators or complimentary public IPv4 addresses are included.

Benchmark evaluations indicate strong multi-core performance and exceptional memory throughput. The server achieved a top-tier rating in both uncached large-block memory read bandwidth (450.77 GB/sec) and write bandwidth (169.21 GB/sec), alongside a top-tier Passmark memory score. Multi-core processing is robust, as demonstrated by strong results in multi-threaded stress-ng CPU tests, Geekbench multi-core scores, and bzip3 multi-threaded decompression. Database operations also rank in the top tier, with Passmark database operations scoring high and Redis SET operations reaching 61.98 million operations per second. However, single-core performance remains average across Geekbench and stress-ng tests. Large-scale LLM inference represents a notable bottleneck, with prompt processing for a 70B model falling into the poor category at 4.66 tokens per second.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the D32plds_v6 offers high resource density for multi-threaded workloads that do not require massive memory-to-vCPU ratios. The 1:2 RAM-to-vCPU ratio positions this instance as a cost-effective option for compute-bound tasks where local storage is required. It is highly suitable for multi-threaded software compilation, web serving, database operations, and intermediate-scale data processing. It is less suited for memory-intensive databases or large-scale LLM inference due to the memory capacity constraints and lower single-core performance.
